# Merged cells with borders in adjacent columns

Original controls generated by tools/merged_adjacent_borders_fixture.py.
The package scaffold is the project's original Latin-ligature control; all table
and text XML here is independently authored, with no corpus artwork or text.
The reference application exported the reference read-only. The local PDF stays
in scratch storage; reference.json records source/PDF hashes and 80 native
text positions. Regenerate it with tools/record_merged_adjacent_borders.py PDF.

Sixteen pages combine automatic/minimum row heights, outer sidebar borders,
a horizontal border in the adjacent column, and zero/nonzero sidebar padding.
The sidebar spans three rows; a centered heading spans the first two. The third
column has two ordinary empty paragraphs with an optional shared 1.5 pt border.
Padded cases use 7.2/3.6 pt top/bottom margins in the first sidebar cell and
3.6/3.6 pt in its continuation cells. Each control has a following-row and an
after-table label so local and accumulated displacement can be distinguished.

Before correction, cases 10 and 14 placed the centered heading about 1.6 pt
and following text about 3 pt too low. The other fourteen controls matched.
The row calculation added the largest margin in one cell to the largest border
in another. Each cell's margin and edge must be combined before taking the row
maximum. A first private candidate using each cell's own bottom declaration
corrected these controls but failed existing unequal opposing-border probes.
The final calculation therefore uses the already-resolved local bottom segment,
including the opposing winner. It reuses the existing resolution pass and
retains the global half-stroke floor and invisible none-border extents.

This refines observed reference layout behavior; it is not a demonstrated conflict
with an explicit normative inset formula. Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses:
17.4.38 tblBorders, 17.4.66 tcBorders, 17.4.68 tcMar, 17.4.80 trHeight,
and the top/bottom margin clauses. The existing row-border-insets and
compound-row-insets controls remain necessary regression references.
